1	/**
2	 * Lakeview Labs & Kidney Care: FOLIO export, version 1.
3	 *
4	 * Lakeview runs an outreach reference laboratory and a nephrology clinic on one system. The export is a
5	 * row-for-row copy of that system's tables. Every payload entry is one table row; its `type` is the table
6	 * name. Column names are the database's own (UPPER_SNAKE). Codes are Lakeview's, documented below; the
7	 * tables at the end of this file list every code value in use.
8	 *
9	 * Two kinds of item, each with its own entry type:
10	 *
11	 * - **Lab report items** (`LabReportRow`): one item per requisition, i.e. one set of specimens drawn at
12	 *   one time for one ordering client. Holds exactly one LAB_REQ row, one LAB_ORDER row per ordered test,
13	 *   and the LAB_RESULT rows those orders produced. Published when every order on the requisition is
14	 *   resulted, cancelled or void (rarely earlier, with 'P' rows, when a slow test holds up a requisition
15	 *   with urgent results). Lab items have no author (system-generated) and no narrative.
16	 * - **Clinic contact items** (`ClinicRow`): one item per nephrology clinic contact (office visit or
17	 *   telephone contact). Holds exactly one CLINIC_VISIT row plus the VISIT_DX, VITAL, MED_ORDER and
18	 *   MED_STATUS_HIST rows entered during that contact. The narrative is the note the nephrologist typed
19	 *   and signed; it is short and is never generated from the rows.
20	 *
21	 * Changes: rows are never edited in place in the export. When a row changes after its item was
22	 * published (a result invalidated, an order marked entered in error), Lakeview publishes a new item that
23	 * `supersedes` the old one and restates every row of the requisition or contact with current values.
24	 * Exception: a medication's status changes are separate MED_STATUS_HIST rows in a later contact, not a
25	 * re-published MED_ORDER row. See MED_ORDER.MED_STATUS.
26	 *
27	 * Times: every timestamp column is RFC 3339 with the UTC offset in effect in America/Chicago at that
28	 * moment (e.g. `2026-02-09T08:14:00-06:00`). Date-only columns are local calendar dates.
29	 *
30	 * Identifiers: REQ_ID, ORDER_ID, RESULT_ID, ACCESSION, VISIT_ID, RX_ID and HIST_ID are Lakeview-assigned,
31	 * never reused, and unique across the whole export (not only within an item). Rows refer to rows in
32	 * other items by these ids.
33	 */
34

`out/transform.ts` is written. It type-checks and runs on the sample patient without errors. I only read the output for as-of 2024-01-01 and only the first part of it (medication, problems, labs, and the first vitals rows). I haven't tested the cases the samples don't contain, such as hidden-only restatements, drug-caused diagnoses and multiple prescriptions for one drug.

Judgment calls:
- **Scope and corrections:** an item is in scope if its `recorded` date in Chicago is on or before `asOf`. Anything named in an in-scope item's `supersedes` or `retracts` is dropped.
- **Labs:**
  - I report results with status F or A as final and P as preliminary. I skip C and X results, and results from orders with status 5 or 9.
  - Comparators are parsed from `VALUE_TEXT`, never from `VALUE_NUM`.
  - K/uL becomes `10*3/uL`.
  - Calculated LDL rows marked X are skipped.
- **eGFR:**
  - I keep `LK-EGFR09N` and `LK-EGFR21` and drop the race-coefficient variant `LK-EGFR09A`.
  - The equation comes from the comment text first, falling back to the code, because the 2009 rows carry MDRD LOINC codes.
  - LOINC is passed through as the source gives it.
- **Medications:**
  - Status is the latest `MED_STATUS_HIST` row for the prescription, otherwise the order's own status.
  - Entered-in-error prescriptions are dropped, including any with an ERR history row, and IV orders are excluded.
  - I keep one row per ingredient, taking the one with the latest event.
  - `status_since` is the date of the last change, or `START_DATE` if there is no history.
  - Stop reasons map ADR to adverse_reaction and PT to patient_choice, and any other code to other.
  - `rxnorm_ingredient` is left out because the source's RxNorm codes are product-level.
- **Problems:**
  - I keep the latest confirmed or historical entry per ICD-10 code, with all N18.x codes treated as one CKD condition.
  - If the latest entry for a condition is "ruled out", I drop the condition. Provisional entries alone never produce a row.
  - The CKD stage and albuminuria come from the latest visit that recorded them.
  - Onset is read only from "since …" text inside the narrative span that cites the diagnosis entry, since the payload has no onset field. Narrative is the only basis for onset in this source.
- **Drug-caused diagnoses:** T-codes and "associated/induced" diagnosis texts produce an allergy row. The reaction type and mechanism are keyword heuristics from the diagnosis text. I did not implement the "one drug of that class on the medication list" substitution, so a class name stays as written.
- **Vitals:** one clinic row per visit, timed at the first BP (or the earliest measurement if there is no BP). Reading 2 of BP goes in the `repeat_*` fields. Weight is rounded to one decimal.
